text: Battery D's mission for April: "Defense of 189th Field Artillery Battalion; Defense of 45th Div. Arty. Cub Air Fields".
source: 106th AAA AW Bn, April 1945 history, p. 2

text: The battalion moves at 1015 to Bergen, just north-west of Neuburg.
source: 189th FA Bn, April 1945 history, typed pp. 246-247

placed: Secondary accounts; not yet checked against a German record
text: Twelve Me 262s of JV 44 take off from Munich-Riem with R4M rockets to attack B-26s.
source: The Aviation Geek Club, drawing on Robert Forsyth's histories of JV 44

text: B-26B-41 42-43311 "Spot Cash", out of Dijon for Lechfeld airfield, lost to "Enemy Aircraft". Last known: "Neuburg, Ger.". A gunner: "His ship ... was hit by ME-262's on their first pass".

"From 1145B to 1147B six (6) ME-262s flying at 500 to 5000 feet attacking B-26 Bombers were engaged by Batteries C and D without result. Ammunition expenditures: 10 rounds 37mm and 159 rounds .50 cal."
source: 106th AAA AW Bn, April 1945 history, p. 6

text: B-26G-25 44-68076 "Big Red" (No. 98) lost to "Enemy Aircraft". Last known 48° 46′ N, 11° 11′ E. The squadron's sketch map has the formation heading south-south-east past Eichstätt and the X just north of Neuburg.

placed: A claim as tabulated from a secondary source
text: Generalleutnant Adolf Galland, commanding JV 44, claims a B-26 "vicinity of Neuburg": his 100th, credited. It was his last mission.
source: Mathews and Foreman, Luftwaffe Aces, vol. 2, p. 366, as tabulated in Wikipedia

text: B-26F 42-96328 (No. 25), typed "B26-F1MA", lost to "Enemy Aircraft". Last known "Neuberg, Germany". A gunner: "It was attacked by a ME-262 from 6 o'clock level ... flames enveloped the ship from cockpit to rear bomb bay". The squadron's sketch map puts it down in the woods at Rohrenfels, south of the Danube.

placed: A claim as tabulated from a secondary source
text: Galland claims a second B-26 "vicinity of Neuburg", unconfirmed.
source: Mathews and Foreman, Luftwaffe Aces, vol. 2, p. 366, as tabulated in Wikipedia

text: "At 1200 we witnessed a sad sight. A formation of American bombers flying directly overhead were attacked by four German jet propelled planes, and three of the bombers were shot down, one of which burst into flame and exploded in the air. One of the German aircraft was downed but the rest got away."
source: 189th FA Bn, April 1945 history, typed pp. 246-247

text: The battalion's command post opens at Wellheim at 1515B.
A single Me 262 is engaged again by Batteries C and D, also without result.
source: 106th AAA AW Bn, April 1945 history, p. 6
